thread:
claire: Heads up 16: I ran a quarterly pattern scan for crashes/restarts. There's a clear recurring theme: memory pressure when multiple large model variants are scheduled on the same node during rolling updates. Putting an action tracker here.

omar: Yep saw that too. Correlation matrix I made: node OOM events spike right after 2nd variant deploys + higher concurrency.

ben: Filing this under 'recurring pattern: model-swap-memory'. Can we quantify how many customers were impacted?

claire: Dashboard link: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/patterns/model-swap-q2. Summary: 17 incidents in last 90 days, 11 had service restarts, 6 resulted in transient 502s seen by callers.

lina: Any quick wins? If we can avoid simultaneous heavy loads during rollout we might mitigate most cases.

omar: Quick win idea: add a soft-scheduler limit preventing >1 large-variant load per GPU at the same time. Could be a scheduler flag. Low effort.

ben: Longer term we should do memory-aware placement and enforce reservation during image/model pull. Also need better observability on per-model memory footprint.

ops-bot: Automated note: tag incidents with `pattern:model-swap-memory` when updating postmortems to help aggregation.

claire: Proposed actions (draft):
- M1: Scheduler: add `max_concurrent_variant_load=1` toggle and rollout to clusters. Owner: omar. Due: 2024-06-02.
- M2: Add pre-reserve memory for model pulls and reject scheduling if reservation fails. Owner: ben. Due: 2024-06-16.
- M3: Capture per-model memory profile in model registry and surface it to placement logic. Owner: lina. Due: 2024-06-30.
- M4: Postmortem updates: annotate all 17 incidents with the new tag + link to this thread. Owner: claire. Due: 2024-05-20.
- M5: Customer comms draft for affected accounts (product + support). Owner: ben. Due: 2024-05-24.

omar: I can take M1. I'll implement the toggle behind a feature flag and do a 2-cluster canary (eu-central, us-east).

lina: M3 in progress  gathering memory traces now. Will push initial registry fields by next week.

ben: Taking M2 and M5. For M5 I'll coordinate with product to soften language.

claire: For M4 I'll run a quick script to bulk-update postmortem metadata. ops-bot please remind folks to add the tag when they edit.

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: 2024-05-18 09:00 UTC to prompt postmortem tagging.

claire: Also thinking we should add an automated alert: when >3 model loads in 5m on same node, create a high-priority paging event to SRE. Any objections?

omar: Strong +1. We got burned by silent memory churn. Alerting will let us intervene before OOM.

lina: Agree. I'll add the metric to the alert rule set once registry data is live.

ben: Small note on rollout order: schedule heavy variants after lighter ones and prefer node-drain approach that respects memory reservation. I'll add details to the scheduler PR.

claire: Ok timeline check: M1/M2 are highest priority. We'll re-evaluate after the canary and update this thread. Weekly status updates please: prepend message with the M-id.

ben: M2 in progress  experimental reservation impl pushed to branch.

omar: M1 planned  feature flag PR opened. Canary run scheduled for 2024-05-22.

lina: M3 in progress  exporting traces now.

claire: Thanks all. We'll use this thread as canonical tracker. Next quick sync Friday 13:30 UTC. If anything urgent, page #eng-oncall.

sre-bot: Note: please add runbook step to fallback to older variant when memory pressure threshold reached.

claire: Added runbook task to M4. Closing for now.
